title: Harvard Astrophysicist Avi Loeb Responds To Elon Musk's Troubling Tweet: 'Why No Sign Of Aliens Yet'
excerpt: The closest potentially habitable planet to Earth, Proxima Centauri b, is about 4.2 light-years away. Yet we have not seen one techno signature from the planet or any tangible evidence of ETs visiting us earthlings. Are they hiding the truth or are we NPCs oblivious to far superior entities and dimensions?
content:
Where is everybody?

The Department of War under the Trump administration released the 7th batch of UFO or UAP files on October 23, 2026. The total documents now in the cache stands at 478 files, including a handful of visual media, that had gotten some excitement momentarily as the tall promises and buzz about the big reveal of aliens never really happened. Most of the documents are already accessible either in the public domain or in shady corners of the internet, including dedicated subreddits. This is not to undermine the efforts of the disclosure project, just that it has been sluggish and been a disappointment in general. And so is the richest billionaire on the planet who has jokingly dubbed himself an extraterrestrial on a few occasions. Reacting to a post on X/Twitter, Elon Musk wrote

“It troubles me greatly that we do not yet see any sign of aliens,”

Certainly he is neither the first nor the last Homo sapiens to have struggled with the vastness of the universe that’s riddled with billions of galaxies and potential exoplanets in the habitable zone of their respective stars, like Proxima b, that is merely 4 light-years away from Earth

Fermi's Paradox

Enrico Fermi, in 1950, during a lunch break, asked what has bugged civilization for ages. Assuming that there are a billion galaxies, surely there must be a handful of intelligent and advanced civilizations with capabilities to travel intergalactically. Then why don't we see them? This, in essence, is dubbed ‘Fermi’s Paradox.’ You can read a good explainer on SETI’s website here.

Sagans Searing Skepticism

During an interview with NOVA, discussing the UFO abduction phenomenon, American astronomer and science communicator Carl Sagan quipped on what would it be like discovering extraterrestrial life in broad daylight with the whole world watching

It would be an absolutely transforming event in human history.

Without overtly dismissing the UFO abduction cases, the skeptic in him emphasized how stakes are high, demanding "rigorous standards of evidence." He also warned about the “contamination by the general culture.” WIth the advent of social media, this phenomenon has been at an all-time high with several conspiracy theories on pop lores from crop circles to flatwoods monsters and underwater UFO bases and the like. So what did science during the days of Carl Sagan have to say about the plausibility of aliens? The maverick remarked.

Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence

He further added,

Extraordinary claims require extraordinary investigations, those investigations must be true to the spirit of science.

Avi Loeb Addresses Musk's Tweet

Do we have evidence at all? Harvard astrophysicist Avi Loeb in his latest blog on the Voyager probe that will soon attain a 'One Light Day' distance from Earth on November 18, 2026, wrote, while reacting to Elon Musk’s aforementioned tweet, a sentiment he has been expressing since the passage of interstellar interloper 3I/ATLAS

When Elon Musk tweeted today here: “It troubles me greatly that we do not yet see any sign of aliens,” echoing Enrico Fermi’s question: “Where is everybody?”, I could not help myself but wonder whether we did not recognize signals from alien technologies because we were not tuned to the possibility that they are out there.

Boy, were we probing it wrong all along? Stay tuned for more in this series.
